text:
maya-ng: FYI customer (acme-app) raised intermittent SSE streams — connection stays open but last few chunks never arrive, client reconnects and sometimes gets duplicate partial payloads. Ticket CS-8791. Happening since ~10:12 UTC.

jon-choi: can you paste server logs + client repro? is this via our edge/proxy or direct to runtime? any auth errors?

maya-ng: edge -> nginx in front (customer's corp proxy). No auth errors. Server logs show a pattern: write attempts succeed then EAGAIN/EPIPE, then connection aborted. sendq grows before failure. snippet: 

```
2026-02-14T10:12:08Z stream-svc[pid=2345] INFO conn=0x7f8a writev 8192 bytes -> 0
2026-02-14T10:12:09Z stream-svc[pid=2345] WARN conn=0x7f8a sendq 65536 drop=0
2026-02-14T10:12:09Z stream-svc[pid=2345] ERROR conn=0x7f8a writev failed: EAGAIN
2026-02-14T10:12:09Z stream-svc[pid=2345] ERROR conn=0x7f8a writev failed: EPIPE
2026-02-14T10:12:09Z stream-svc[pid=2345] INFO conn=0x7f8a closed by peer
```

maya-ng: metrics: socket_sendq spikes to ~120KB, tcp_retransmits small, client observed 2-3 reconnects in ~30s window. Billing metric shows duplicated tokens during reconnects.

samir: looks like classic slow-consumer/backpressure. Because the customer's nginx has `proxy_buffering on` it buffers our chunks until full and then client stalls. When buffer fills our runtime hits EAGAIN. Can you confirm nginx conf on client side? Also check if `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` is preserved across proxy.

jon-choi: repro suggestion for customer/dev to run a direct curl to bypass proxy: 

```
curl -N -H 'Accept: text/event-stream' 'https://api.redwood-inference.internal/v1/stream?model=ver1' --compressed
```

jon-choi: and try with `--no-buffer` and also with a small keepalive: `--keepalive-time 2` — if direct stream is smooth it's likely proxy buffering.

maya-ng: I asked customer to try and they said direct to runtime reduces partials a lot. When we flip nginx `proxy_buffering off` they see continuous chunks rather than stalled ones.

samir: temporary mitigations: 1) ask proxy owner to `proxy_buffering off` + `proxy_busy_buffers_size` tuned, 2) on runtime reduce write chunk size and flush more frequently, e.g., `max_chunk_bytes=4096`, `flush_interval_ms=50`, 3) increase SO_SNDBUF (try 256KB) and enable TCP_CORK/TCP_NODELAY tuning; 4) enable prefix/KV caching to shrink payloads. Also add server-side backpressure metrics to alert earlier.

jon-choi: engineering action: I'll open eng-runtime canary to change defaults for streaming route. Example rollout payload for console API: 

```
PATCH /runtime/config/streaming
{
  "route": "customer/acme-app",
  "max_chunk_bytes": 4096,
  "flush_interval_ms": 50,
  "so_sndbuf": 262144
}
```

maya-ng: noted. Customer also flagged billing — they were charged for duplicate tokens during reconnect window. Karen, can billing hold any disputed charges while we investigate? @karen-billing

karen-billing: thanks @maya-ng — I've flagged CS-8791 and put a temporary invoice hold for the affected interval. We'll reconcile after engineering confirms duplicate-work behavior.

sre-bot: auto-alert: stream_sendq > 100KB observed on 3 nodes for route customer/acme-app between 10:11-10:15 UTC. Created incident INC-3314.

maya-ng: escalation plan: 1) ask customer to set `proxy_buffering off` as short-term, 2) roll runtime canary with smaller chunks + increased SO_SNDBUF, 3) add alerting for socket_sendq > 64KB, 4) billing hold applied. I'll attach traces and pcap from the customer's repro to INC-3314.

jon-choi: one more note — if the customer cannot change proxy, we should offer Dedicated/VPC route for sensitive streaming workloads; it avoids third-party buffering and gives predictable network path.

maya-ng: thanks everyone — passing to eng-runtime and support follow-up. Will update ticket CS-8791 and ping when canary is live. :thumbsup:
